subjects.description: small red rectangular block attached to the bottom of a vertical spring

observation.what_happens: A red block attached to a vertical spring oscillates up and down in the center of the frame. It starts near its lowest position, then rises and falls repeatedly throughout the clip without being caught or stopping.

reasoning: s moves ~220 pixels vertically with period ~0.7 s (~9 rad/s) and near-constant amplitude, classic vertical spring-mass. Slight amplitude change over 4.5 s motivates viscous and quadratic air-drag damping, and large stretch motivates a cubic Duffing nonlinearity test.

truth.note: This clip was rendered from a law drawn by public randomness (drand round 6604982) and sealed before the run: its SHA-256 was committed and pushed in 4b94c8b, the law revealed in 9997e76. Missed. The drawn law was a lopsided (asymmetric) spring with viscous damping and a periodic drive. Muse Wonder, called in by code because the best law missed the fitted frames by 102 times the noise, wrote two independent modes: an undamped one at the drive's own frequency (15.21 ± 0.27 against 15.22 rad/s) and a damped one near the spring's. That is how a driven linear spring moves, but it is not a drive term, and the lopsided stiffness was not found. With no ruler found, lengths are in pixels; true values in pixels use the render's own scale.

drawn.equation: x'' = -(k/m) x - (k2/m) x^2 - b x' + F0 cos(wd t)
drawn.x: displacement below the resting point (m, down positive); t from release

k2.rule: k2 A / k uniform in [0.2, 0.45], stiffer stretched (drawn 0.283)

F0.rule: F0 / |w0^2 - wd^2| = share of A uniform in [0.15, 0.35] (drawn 0.238)

wd.rule: wd / w0 uniform in [0.55, 0.8] or [1.25, 1.6], each half the time (drawn 1.561)
